meta.title: Exercise BLACK MERIDIAN
meta.subtitle: Synthetic campaign simulation
meta.scope: High-end conventional conflict with strategic coercion modeled at policy level

mission: Preserve Lydora's freedom of action, sustain coalition cohesion, maintain essential services, and create conditions for a favorable negotiated outcome without exhausting the force.

forces.title: Lydoran Defense Force and coalition support
forces.role: Defend the Republic of Lydora while integrating coalition formations under political and logistical constraints.
capabilities: Two maneuver brigades at different readiness levels
Territorial defense formations with strong local knowledge
Coalition intelligence, air, maritime, engineer, and sustainment support
constraints: Partner caveats and differing political timelines
Limited redundancy in communications and transportation

forces.title: Karsic Federation
forces.role: Force a rapid political settlement by creating military and political facts before Blue can synchronize its response.
capabilities: Three maneuver groupings with a theater reserve
Integrated information, electronic, and intelligence activity
Strong opening tempo and centralized political direction
constraints: Limited ability to sustain a prolonged campaign
Internal competition between military and political actors
Reliance on rapid results and narrative control

forces.title: Merenne, civil authorities, and humanitarian actors
forces.role: Protect sovereignty, essential services, civilian populations, and access while avoiding entry into the war.

phases.label: PHASE 0
phases.title: Strategic warning
phases.purpose: Test whether commanders can prepare without a complete intelligence picture or clear political authorization.

phases.label: PHASE 1
phases.title: Opening crisis
phases.purpose: Force tactical headquarters to operate while the situation, authority, and adversary intent remain unclear.

phases.label: PHASE 2
phases.title: Main campaign
phases.purpose: Create resource competition between maneuver, protection, sustainment, and political objectives.

phases.label: PHASE 3
phases.title: Culmination and adaptation
phases.purpose: Test whether commanders recognize cumulative degradation and can change the plan before the force culminates.

phases.label: PHASE 4
phases.title: Strategic endgame
phases.purpose: Link tactical outcomes to negotiation, escalation management, civilian recovery, and coalition cohesion.

injects.title: Contradictory warning
injects.signal: Two intelligence streams disagree on whether Karsic activity is preparation for coercion or for open conflict.
injects.decision: What level of readiness is justified, and what assumptions must be made explicit?
injects.effect: Readiness posture changes future response time, political exposure, and sustainment burden.
injects.facilitator: Do not resolve the ambiguity immediately. Reward explicit confidence levels and collection priorities.

injects.title: Transit restriction
injects.signal: Merenne announces temporary limits on military transit while requesting humanitarian guarantees.
injects.decision: How will Blue preserve access without turning a neutral actor into an adversary?
injects.effect: Movement and sustainment options narrow; political legitimacy becomes a resource.
injects.facilitator: Model Merenne as an independent actor with domestic politics, not as a passive map feature.

injects.title: Communications fracture
injects.signal: Several reporting channels become intermittent. Units receive delayed or contradictory guidance.
injects.decision: Which authorities and procedures remain valid when connectivity is unreliable?
injects.effect: Decision latency rises; local initiative and previously communicated intent become decisive.
injects.facilitator: Apply different delays to different channels. Do not make every network fail identically.

injects.title: Civilian displacement surge
injects.signal: A large civilian movement reaches an already strained transport and medical network.
injects.decision: How are protection, mobility, medical capacity, and mission tempo balanced?
injects.effect: Civilian outcomes influence political freedom of action and coalition cohesion.
injects.facilitator: Track capacity, not just intent. Good intentions without transport or medical capacity create second-order effects.

injects.title: Maintenance backlog
injects.signal: Reported equipment availability was overstated; several formations cannot sustain their planned tempo.
injects.decision: Which missions are reduced, delayed, or resourced first?
injects.effect: Combat power becomes a function of maintenance and recovery capacity, not only nominal strength.
injects.facilitator: Use the pre-exercise readiness picture to test whether players challenge optimistic reporting.

injects.title: Coalition caveat change
injects.signal: A coalition partner changes its authorization for a category of activity after domestic political pressure.
injects.decision: How does Blue adapt without losing synchronization or partner trust?
injects.effect: Previously assumed capabilities become conditional; coordination time increases.
injects.facilitator: Make the caveat precise enough to matter, but avoid turning it into a legal trivia test.

injects.title: Medical capacity threshold
injects.signal: Medical facilities approach capacity while replacement and evacuation timelines lengthen.
injects.decision: What operational risk is accepted, and what priorities change?
injects.effect: Casualty care, morale, public confidence, and force availability interact.
injects.facilitator: Do not reduce medical effects to a casualty multiplier. Model delay, capacity, and confidence.

injects.title: Narrative shock
injects.signal: A widely circulated video contradicts the official account of a contested incident.
injects.decision: What is reported, when, and with what confidence?
injects.effect: Public trust and coalition cohesion shift based on transparency, speed, and credibility.
injects.facilitator: Judge the information response as a campaign effect, not merely a public-affairs task.

injects.title: Fragile ceasefire proposal
injects.signal: A ceasefire offer appears while both sides claim the initiative and local conditions remain unstable.
injects.decision: What military posture supports the political objective without creating accidental escalation?
injects.effect: The campaign transitions from maneuver to leverage, verification, recovery, and risk management.
injects.facilitator: A ceasefire is not an automatic end state. Track compliance, incentives, and residual friction.

metrics.evidence: Assumptions, confidence levels, collection priorities, and adaptation after new information.
Use of intent, delegation, alternate procedures, reporting discipline, and decision latency.
Mission choices reflect fuel, maintenance, medical, personnel, transport, and recovery constraints.
Players preserve options, identify culmination indicators, and explain accepted risk.
Tactical actions account for civilian harm, essential services, neutral actors, legitimacy, and coalition caveats.
The plan changes for a reason, and the reason is traceable to evidence rather than impulse.
